title: Batting Partnerships as Networks: Mapping Rajasthan Royals’s Run Creation
dek: Runs are made in pairs. Treating Rajasthan Royals' partnerships as a network shows which batters hold the order together and how concentrated the run-making really is.
excerpt: Since 2022, Rajasthan Royals have used many batting pairs, but the five most productive account for a large share of partnership runs. YBK Jaiswal sits at the centre of the network.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Batting as a Network
body: Each batter is a node; each partnership is a link weighted by the runs the pair added. The shape of the network shows whether a side relies on one great pair or spreads the work.
Since 2022, Rajasthan Royals have used {{ev:pn-pairs}} distinct batting pairs.

sections.heading: The Strongest Links
body: The most productive pair is {{ev:pn-top-pair}}, with {{ev:pn-top-r}} runs together. The five most productive pairs account for {{ev:pn-share}} of all partnership runs.
The chart lists the leading pairs and their run rate together.

sections.heading: The Hubs
body: {{ev:pn-hub}} is involved in more partnership runs than anyone, {{ev:pn-hub-r}}. {{ev:pn-mostp}} has batted with the most different partners, {{ev:pn-mostp-n}}, a sign of a flexible role.

sections.heading: Method Notes
body: Partnership runs include extras and are counted from the ball-by-ball record, using the striker and non-striker on each delivery.
The network describes who batted together, not why; batting order and match situation shape it heavily.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Protect the Hubs
body: Rajasthan Royals' run-making is concentrated around a few pairs and a central hub. Losing the hub would disrupt more partnerships than losing any other batter.
That is a case for planning his replacement before it is needed.
